title: Bounded-space search returns the correct answer
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine deciding a language $L$ within space bound $sp$, and let $x$ be a Boolean string. For all natural numbers $d,s$ and all Boolean memories $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, suppose $sp(|x|)-s=d$, $s\le sp(|x|)$, and every $z$ with $M(z)=\mathrm{true}$ satisfies $z<2\,kb(N,|x|,s)$. Then the exponential breadth-first-search program, started with radius $s$, logarithm register $lgv(|x|)$, all other registers zero, memory $M$, and memory head at $0$, halts with the correct answer to whether $x\in L$. Every configuration before halting satisfies the program guard with register bound $bigB(N,|x|,sp(|x|))$ and memory-head position between $0$ and $3\,kb(N,|x|,sp(|x|)+1)$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: true memory positions lie strictly below $2\,kb(N,|x|,s)$
replaced:
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine deciding a language $L$ within
space bound $sp$, and let $x$ be a binary input. For every $d,s\in\mathbb{N}$ and memory
contents $M:\mathbb{Z}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, suppose $sp(|x|)-s=d$, $s\le
sp(|x|)$, and every position $z$ marked true by $M$ satisfies $z<2\,kb(N,|x|,s)$. Then
the specified exponential breadth-first-search machine, started with radius $s$,
logarithmic register initialized to $lgv(|x|)$, all other registers zero, memory $M$,
and memory head at $0$, halts with output $1$ exactly when $x\in L$ (and output $0$
otherwise), while satisfying its configuration guard with register bound
$bigB(N,|x|,sp(|x|))$ and memory-head bound $3\,kb(N,|x|,sp(|x|)+1)$. The machine's
oracle is the four-language decider derived from $N$, and the reachability assertion
uses that the intermediate configurations satisfy the stated guard.
